ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA appeared in all 6 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction — the strongest signal in today's digest. As the last Mag-7 name to report, the August 26 earnings event is a hard-dated catalyst with consensus Q2 revenue at $93.63B (revised up 6.67% in 90 days, with BofA outlier at $94–95B) and a $303 average analyst price target vs. ~$225 current price — a ~34.6% gap. Despite hypergrowth, NVDA's forward P/E of 34.3x sits at a 44% discount to its own 10-year average of 61.6x, creating a fundamental re-rating argument; a debit call spread expiring early September captures binary upside while defining downside risk ahead of the Jackson Hole macro event two days later.
ideas.catalyst: Q2 FY2027 earnings report August 26, 2026 (after market close); Jackson Hole Fed keynote August 28 as secondary macro risk
ideas.edge: Consensus PT $302.83 vs. ~$225 current (~34.6% upside gap); Q2 revenue consensus $93.63B revised up 6.67% in 3 months; forward P/E 34.3x is a 44% discount to 10-year average of 61.6x; 41/41 (or 58/61) analysts rate Buy
ideas.bull_case: A beat-and-raise above the $103B Q3 consensus — driven by accelerating Blackwell shipments and HBM4 demand — could rapidly close the gap to the $303 analyst target and trigger a historic P/E re-rating toward the 10-year average.
ideas.bear_case: Elevated expectations after 95%+ YoY growth guidance leave little room for error; any supply constraint commentary, export restriction escalation, or hawkish Warsh surprise on Aug 28 could trigger a sharp post-earnings reversal despite solid numbers.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. (ADR)
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 6 overnight screens — tied with NVDA for perfect consensus — as the purest US-listed vehicle for HBM4 AI memory demand. The stock recently IPO'd on Nasdaq at $149 (July 2026) and remains in price discovery with limited US analyst coverage despite a $500B+ confirmed NVIDIA–SK Group AI infrastructure pact, record Q2 operating margin of 76%, and 257% YoY revenue growth. The consensus analyst target of $245.46 vs. a current range of ~$143–$168 implies 45–70% upside, and NVDA's August 26 earnings serve as a direct read-through catalyst for HBM demand confirmation. Stock entry is preferred over options given thin post-IPO options liquidity; a defined stop near the $149 IPO price manages downside.

ideas.edge: Consensus analyst PT $245.46 vs. ~$143–$168 current range (45–70% upside gap); record Q2 76% operating margin and 257% YoY revenue growth; $500B+ NVIDIA partnership confirmed; new Nasdaq listing creates valuation gap vs. Korean-listed peers due to limited US coverage
ideas.bull_case: An NVDA earnings beat on August 26 confirming accelerating HBM4 orders, combined with formal supply contract announcements from the South Korean presidential visit, could rapidly compress the gap to the $245 analyst target from its price-discovery discount.
ideas.bear_case: As a newly listed ADR, SKHY has demonstrated 8–11% single-session drawdowns on geopolitical headlines; a South Korea–US trade dispute escalation, NVDA earnings miss, or broader risk-off following a hawkish Warsh speech could trigger outsized volatility relative to the underlying fundamentals.

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust (Nasdaq-100 ETF)

VIX at 14.25 — near multi-month lows — makes near-dated options historically cheap heading into a known two-event volatility cluster: NVDA earnings (August 26) and Fed Chair Warsh's first-ever Jackson Hole keynote (August 28), where a September rate hike is >60% priced. Deteriorating consumer sentiment (51.0, down from 55.2) and S&P 500 at all-time highs with crowded long positioning amplify the asymmetry; a straddle or put spread expiring August 29 captures both events in a single defined-cost structure.
ideas.catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole keynote August 28, 2026; NVDA earnings August 26 as the Nasdaq-100's largest single-stock risk event; FOMC decision September 16
ideas.edge: VIX at 14.25 (near multi-month low) makes options cheapest heading into the highest-uncertainty Fed event of the year; two binary macro events within 48 hours; September rate hike >60% priced vs. market consensus leaning dovish — positioning asymmetry favors vol buyers
ideas.bull_case: A dovish Warsh surprise (signaling a September pause) combined with an NVDA blowout would propel QQQ to new highs, making the straddle structure profitable on the upside leg while the put spread expires worthless — a low-cost hedge that incidentally benefits from a melt-up.
ideas.bear_case: If Warsh delivers an unexpectedly hawkish message or signals a September hike, tech multiples at all-time highs and crowded AI positioning could unwind sharply; the put spread structure profits in this scenario, but a gradual grind higher with no vol expansion would cause the options to decay without a directional payoff.

ideas.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund
ideas.thesis: XLE appeared in 2 of 6 overnight screens — meeting the minimum threshold — as a sector hedge and geopolitical risk play. The 2.4% dividend yield provides carry while holding.
